[[Category:Transformer]]
'''KV caching''' is a technique to reduce computational cost during [[large language model (LLM)#Typical_implementation:_sequential_next_token_prediction|sequential next token prediction]] in [[Transformer]]s by caching the attention keys and values computed for earlier tokens for use in calculation of later tokens.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3192}}</ref>

== Compute without KV caching ==

To generate an [[token (machine learning)|output token sequence]] of length $T$ via [[large language model (LLM)#Typical_implementation:_sequential_next_token_prediction|sequential next token prediction]]:

At step $t$ the model evaluates attention (e.g., [[self-attention]]) over the first $t$ tokens processed so far, at cost $O(t^2d)$, where $d$ is the '''hidden dimension''' of the attention mechanism.

Overall compute:

$$
\sum_{t=1}^{T}O(t^2d)=O(T^3 d)
$$

where $O$ is the [[o(x) and o(x)|big-O notation]].

== Compute with KV caching ==

With the cache in place, each step scores only the 1 new token against the $t$ stored keys and values, at cost $O(td)$, and the total becomes

$$
\sum_{t=1}^{T}O(td)=O(T^2 d),
$$

== Memory tradeoff ==

[[File:KV caching.png|thumbnail|300px|As the [[context window (Sequential token generation)|context window]] of [[LLM]]s grow larger, approaching or exceeding $10^6$ tokens in 2026, the memory cost of '''KV caching''' can itself become a bottleneck.]]
$$
|\mathbf{K}|+|\mathbf{V}|=2Td
$$

scalars per layer.

Which means, memory size required for full caching grows linearly with the length of the generated sequence.

<ref>{{#cite:Q3207}}</ref>
